diagnostic_science_review_20261009.scope_note: Comparison enrichment only; no canonical installation or gallery backfill. Genus project_scope's eight-species B061 cohort is historical, NOT the full canonical roster. Manifest audit on 2026-10-09: 17 installed Oenothera IDs. look_here_first: Sort the specimen by flower architecture: classic radial primrose, minute-flowered former-Gaura spike, showier former-Gaura spike, or yellow sundrop (former Calylophus).
Inspect flower and bud side views, including hypanthium, sepal tips, and inferior ovary; do not classify from petal color.
For former-Gaura spikes compare flowering-axis hairs at magnification, open-flower diameter, and mature indehiscent fruit proportions.
For sundrops compare lower versus upper leaves, bud tip length, sepal keels, hypanthium, and stigma; verify the subspecies concept before merging historical names.
Confirm using mature capsule/fruit and multiple organs. A single worn flower, color, habitat, or photo without scale is not a safe separator.

pair: Oenothera capillifolia subsp. berlandieri (source alias Calylophus berlandieri)
comparison_groups.title: Former Calylophus subspecies identity — DO NOT AUTO-MERGE

diagnostics.detail: POWO accepts O. capillifolia subsp. berlandieri for Calylophus berlandieri Spach; separately accepts O. capillifolia subsp. capillifolia. Species-level O. capillifolia learner is not evidence of subspecies identity.

UT Williamson County subsp. capillifolia has narrow leaves about 20–75 × 1.2–3 mm, conspicuously four-sided buds, and 28–40 mm open flowers; these are an anchor, not a validated dichotomous separator from berlandieri.
FNA gives 30–80 cm erect/ascending stems, leaves 2.5–9 × 0.2–1 cm, free bud tips 0.5–4 mm, and keeled sepals. These ranges overlap some sundrops and are not an independent diagnosis without full key.

unreliable: A dark purple floral tube or stigma occurs in FNA-documented subsp. capillifolia populations from Hays and neighboring counties: DO NOT use dark tube/stigma color to force berlandieri.
Texas nativity at the species/subspecies level does not establish a project three-county native PASS for an unidentified source record.
Source label 'Calylophus berlandieri' must not automatically be attached to a photograph labeled subsp. capillifolia.

Preserve source-pool learner admission but mark exact mapping HOLD; do not create a new canonical card, silently fold the name into O. serrulata, or infer native PASS.

comparison_groups.title: Stemless long-tube rosette

diagnostics.detail: Acaulescent flat basal rosette with stem concealed at ground level, unlike tall leafy stems of many other primroses.
Very long, sharply four-angled hypanthium to approximately 97 mm in UT Williamson County description; trace it all the way to the inferior ovary.
UT Williamson County detailed dissection reports four stamens; use as a corroborating dissected-flower feature, not a stand-alone identification when counts conflict across sources.

unreliable: Yellow petals and lobed leaves are shared by multiple Oenothera.
Stamen counts from a photo or non-dissected worn flower are error-prone.
photo_roles: Full basal rosette with scale and stem position labeled
Whole intact flower side view with ruler spanning hypanthium
Flower dissection clearly exposing stamens and inferior ovary

visual_lesson.title: Evening primroses and former gauras: identify the floral architecture
visual_lesson.intro: LOOK HERE FIRST: sort by radial primrose, airy former-Gaura spike, or former-Calylophus sundrop. On an intact fresh flower trace petals and sepals down the hypanthium to the inferior ovary; then compare flowering-axis hairs and mature fruit. Do not identify from pink/yellow color alone.
visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole flowering architecture → intact hypanthium and ovary → flowering-axis hairs and open flower size → ripe fruit shape and bud/sepal keels

steps.title: 1 · Sort the flowering architecture
steps.photo_role: matched flowering stalks of radial primrose, former-Gaura, and sundrop; not interchangeable generic blooms
steps.look_for: A spreading radial O. speciosa flower, an airy former-Gaura spike, and a yellow sundrop may all belong to Oenothera. Trace the flower attachment and entire flowering axis before choosing a comparison group.
steps.why_it_matters: Modern Oenothera includes former Gaura and Calylophus; petals alone hide these very different structural groups.

steps.title: 2 · Follow the flower tube to the ovary
steps.photo_role: installed exact-species reference, tube anatomy not visually certified; complete scaled side macro needed
steps.look_for: In O. triloba, a basal rosette supports a very long sharply four-angled floral tube; photograph the entire side view including where the ovary sits below the perianth. Compare free sepal tips and keels in sundrops.
steps.why_it_matters: A complete side profile distinguishes the extremely long-tubed rosette group from many stemmed primroses; the floral tube is not the ovary.
steps.image_credit: Sam Kieschnick · CC BY (version and exact reuse terms to reconfirm)

steps.title: 3 · Compare hairs on the FLOWERING axis
steps.photo_role: installed exact-species private-study reference; matched hair macro needed
steps.look_for: At 10×, O. curtiflora has a densely velvety flowering axis and flowers around 3 mm wide; O. suffulta has an essentially glabrous flowering axis and 12–19 mm flowers. Do not judge hairs on leaves alone.
steps.why_it_matters: These separate similar former-Gaura annuals even when both have hairy vegetative stems and white-to-pink petals.
steps.image_credit: Glass Root Garden · direct owner authorization for private study only; no public CC grant

steps.title: 4 · Measure ripe fruits and sundrop buds
steps.photo_role: matched ripe O. curtiflora/O. suffulta fruits plus voucher-confirmed O. capillifolia bud side macros with millimeter scale
steps.look_for: O. curtiflora fruit approximately 8 × 2.7–3 mm, narrow and hairy; O. suffulta 6–7 × 4–6 mm, thick four-lobed and glabrous. For former Calylophus, photograph intact bud side and free sepal tip without assuming subspecies from tube color.
steps.why_it_matters: Mature fruit proportions and bud structure resolve look-alikes that overlap in flower color and general habit.
